method: v2.1 component model: each of the 21 gauge components gets its own 12-month path from the most forward-looking data we hold (for fuel, only the wholesale gasoline pass-through the pump has not yet absorbed — the two-week pump forward shown in the fuel panel plus any 30-day gap beyond it, no trailing momentum; futures curves for food/natgas, wholesale leads for vehicles, new-lease rents for shelter, own trailing medians elsewhere — complete months only), aggregated with CPI weights into index levels; YoY is computed against actual year-ago levels so base effects are exact. Band = the gauge’s own realized monthly volatility × √horizon. The dotted baseline shows a flat 2%-annualized path — everything between it and today’s YoY is pure base-effect arithmetic. History months are the YoY as published (method v1.4 before 2026-09-28); the path and its year-ago bases are on method v1.5, so part of the step between the last published month before the switch and the path is the method change. The official CPI path starts at the Nowflation Forecast for the September 2026 CPI (3.6%), the published call for that print, and after it follows the monthly steps of the Gauge variant built on official shelter, the one that tracks the print.
disclaimer: A model projection, not a promise and not investment advice. Assumptions above; construction versioned in the public changelog; graded against reality on the scoreboard.
